claims.text: High-purity alumina refractory ceramics can be used to fabricate parts for hot-dip aluminum dipping and plating equipment.
Replacing conventional metal components with high-purity alumina ceramics will significantly reduce molten-aluminum-induced corrosion and erosion.
Conventional metal or alloy components are susceptible to rapid corrosion and erosion during long-term contact with high-temperature molten aluminum.
High-purity alumina has a stable, dense microstructure.
The phase purity of high-purity alumina helps form a robust physical barrier against molten aluminum.
The alumina barrier minimizes chemical interactions with molten aluminum.
High-purity alumina exhibits excellent chemical inertness toward molten aluminum.
High-purity alumina has a very high melting point.
The inertness and high melting point of alumina reduce wetting and reaction with molten aluminum.
Reduced reaction with molten aluminum prevents dissolution and erosion of alumina protective parts.
High-purity alumina maintains mechanical integrity under hot-dip aluminum plating operating conditions.
Using high-purity alumina will decrease component corrosion and erosion rates relative to conventional metals or alloys.
The reduced corrosion and erosion rates will extend component service life.
Mechanical stresses, thermal shock, and cyclic loading may impair the protective performance of high-purity alumina.
Rapid temperature changes and cyclic mechanical loading can induce microcracking in high-purity alumina components.
The long-term mechanical durability of high-purity alumina under cyclic thermal and mechanical stresses remains insufficiently validated.
